title: Why We Don’t Need More Data Centers - Dr. Jasper Zhang, Hyperbolic
talk_summary: A pitch for Hyperbolic's GPU marketplace/aggregation layer (HyperDOS, a Kubernetes agent installed on any cluster) that pools idle GPU capacity to cut rental costs 50-75% versus on-demand clouds. The core argument is that low utilization and fragmented supply, not insufficient data centers, drive compute cost, and that elastic rent/release beats long reservations.

takeaways.technique: Elastic capacity rent/release instead of long reservations
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of reserving fixed capacity for a year, rent the baseline and burst extra capacity only for the months needed, then release idle capacity back to the pool.
takeaways.evidence_quote: in month six then I can say okay I can release my idle GPUs on hyperbolic and try to sell
takeaways.numbers: cost reduced from $43.8M to $6.9M (~6x) in their worked example

takeaways.what_they_do: A single orchestration layer (HyperDOS, a Kubernetes agent) sits over many heterogeneous providers so users pick by price/rating/benchmark instead of vetting each supplier.
Argues the real lever is raising utilization of already-paid capacity rather than buying more; idle capacity is the waste.
takeaways.evidence_quote: GPU sit idle 80% of the time for enterprises and companies

takeaways.what_they_do: Marketplace matches fragmented demand to fragmented supply so neither sits idle; the 'matching problem' is the product.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we got kind of like solve the e uh like the matching problem of compute
